title: First cotangent homology vanishing reduces to finite subfields
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be a field extension. Suppose $H_1(L_{E/k})=0$ for every intermediate field $E$ finitely generated as a field over $k$. Then $H_1(L_{L/k})=0$. Here $H_1$ is the kernel of the naive cotangent differential for the canonical polynomial presentation [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), finite-support proof specialized to the union of finitely generated intermediate fields; applied in Tag 0320 (3).

proof.text: Represent a first-homology class by a polynomial g in the kernel I of k[L] → L, with evaluated partial derivatives zero. Its finitely many variables generate a finitely generated intermediate field E. Regard g as a polynomial in k[E] by injective variable renaming.

Evaluation and partial differentiation commute with variable renaming. Injectivity of E → L shows that g and its partial derivatives evaluate to zero in E. Thus g modulo I_E² is a first-homology class for E; it is zero by hypothesis, so g lies in I_E².
Variable renaming sends I_E into I and products into products, so g lies in I² and the original class is zero. Every class is zero, hence first homology is a subsingleton.
